chunks: And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Virtue (al-Birr) and charity (Sadaqah) remove poverty and increase lifespan, and they ward off seventy types of unpleasant deaths for their owner.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of charity and good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the dual efficacy of al-Birr and Sadaqah, noting that they not only alleviate material poverty and extend lifespan but also serve as a divine shield against seventy distinct types of calamitous deaths. This narration underscores the Shia understanding of charity as a comprehensive mechanism for both worldly preservation and spiritual protection, reinforcing the concept of *dafa' al-bala'* (averting calamity) through righteous giving.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 11. And from the previous chain from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from Ishaq b. Ghalib from the one the person that narrated to him from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “
Good deeds and Sadaqah keep poverty away, increases life. A person who does good deeds and gives Sadaqah is safe from seventy types of unpleasant deaths.”
